The sensitisation exercise took place on Tuesday at the NYSC Permanent Orientation Camp, Issele-Uku, Aniocha North Local Government Area, as part of the 2026 NYSC Sensitisation Seminar.
Speaking on the theme, “Save Smart: Choose Insured Institutions and Know Your Cover”, an Assistant Director in the NDIC Examination Unit, Mr Alfonso Chibuzor, said the corporation provides insurance coverage of up to N5 million per depositor in each insured bank.
He explained that the coverage applied to a customer’s total eligible deposits at a single bank, regardless of the number of accounts held. Chibuzor said a customer with N6 million in savings and current accounts in the same bank would receive a maximum insured payout of N5 million if the bank failed.
He advised corps members to confirm that financial institutions were licensed by the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) and insured by the NDIC before depositing their money.
He also warned against assuming that all digital wallets, financial applications and investment products were covered by deposit insurance. Chibuzor explained that the NDIC protects depositors, supervises insured institutions and manages failed banks to strengthen confidence in the banking system.
He identified the CBN’s prudential regulation, supervision and lender-of-last-resort functions as complementary measures for maintaining financial stability.
On deposit reimbursement, he urged customers to maintain accurate banking records and identification details, including their Bank Verification Number (BVN), to facilitate claims verification.
He also advised depositors to obtain information about bank failures and reimbursement procedures through official NDIC channels rather than rely on rumours and unverified social media reports.
In another presentation with title, “Soft Life or Smart Life”, the NDIC Head of Communication, Lagos, Mr Toke Afolayon, urged corps members to embrace financial discipline rather than succumb to pressure to maintain lifestyles beyond their means.”
He described unsustainable spending, compulsory social outings and borrowing to impress others as features of an unhealthy lifestyle.
Afolayon advocated budgeting, regular savings, responsible spending and long-term financial planning.
He urged corps members to cultivate sound financial habits early, stressing that living within their means was essential to achieving financial independence and stability.
He added that they could enjoy life without jeopardising their financial future through responsible money management.
